collectionMethod: Synchronous file reads and imported data modules; deterministic for unchanged source and HEAD. No reachability or render checks are run.
scope: Non-atomic working-tree snapshot, including concurrent edits. Not a release certification or a claim about historical checks.

stations.name: Helios Station
stations.chartNote: Everything in stock, everything watched. Fair prices, constant questions.

stations.name: Coalition HQ
stations.chartNote: Concord's desk. Clean contracts, and a clean record while you're docked.

discoveryPlate.title: SV-3 / Kinetic Choir
discoveryPlate.body: Three loose resonators and a moth-winged survey machine. Scan the conductor; Massline a bell, pull, and release. The chart marks the rehearsal site, not the moving band.

discoveryPlate.title: What Was the Pit?
discoveryPlate.body: Twenty-four candles burn around a deliberately dark twenty-fifth plinth. Its black-box record carries one telemetry smear on the Pit convoy's final course.

discoveryPlate.title: Outer Yard Decommission Frame
discoveryPlate.body: The stripped structural rib of an early transport berth, towed into the outer debris cluster when Helios Station expanded. Cold welds and cutting torch scars mark where the modular gantry was salvaged.

discoveryPlate.title: Bonded Cold Locker
discoveryPlate.body: A pressurized ore-sample locker anchored to the starter seam bedrock. Heavy Concord inspection seals from the initial Helios survey remain intact over an untouched specimen compartment.

discoveryPlate.title: Bay 7 — Shelved Grid
discoveryPlate.body: A maintenance pad the station still files tickets for. The odor is consistent with transit. No action.

discoveryPlate.title: Span-Hold 9
discoveryPlate.body: A claim pin burned down to its own socket. The SPAN-HOLD partnership registered this rock in the first Ceres rush, lapsed, and left the pin to cook in the sun. Its ash line still reads on a scanner as a lane marker, which is more than the partnership ever got back.

discoveryPlate.title: The Whistle
discoveryPlate.body: A decommissioned approach horn cut loose when the yard frame came down. Its residual charge ticks one flat note across the approach band; the yard logs it as weather, and the weather has never once objected.

discoveryPlate.title: The Pit Line
discoveryPlate.body: Sealed relief pods hold formation along a dead-straight drift line, nose-on to the old toll cut. The convoy ran dark to slip it, and the escort was sold on before the rendezvous. A recall notice, re-stamped and redirected, is still lashed to the lead pod. One compartment reads full.

discoveryPlate.title: Checkpoint Niner
discoveryPlate.body: A Concord interdiction buoy holding the mid-chord between the trade ring and Coalition HQ. The scale weighs everything twice here — ore out, resumes in. The lamp has been green for eleven months, and nobody left on the roster remembers who to ask about a yellow one.

discoveryPlate.title: Smear Marker 7
discoveryPlate.body: A survey pin with chalk on the flanks: one arrow, no number, laid on the bearing that runs from the Candle Fleet out toward the rim. Whoever drew it pressed hard enough to score the metal, and then never filed the leg.

pois.name: Shift Bell 3
pois.chartNote: A horn on the Ceres leg. Rings at the end of third shift; first shift has never heard it.

discoveryPlate.title: Shift Bell 3
discoveryPlate.body: A brass relay buoy the harbour rings to end third shift. The bell log lists it as decommissioned twice; the night crews list it as the only clock that matters. It rings on the Ceres heading because that is the leg the ore scows take home.

pois.name: Misdeclared Marker 12-K
pois.chartNote: A transit marker broadcasting the wrong mass. Two corrections filed; the buoy kept the first one.

discoveryPlate.title: Marker 12-K
discoveryPlate.body: A lane marker filed at fourteen tonnes that has always broadcast forty-one. Customs corrected the record in triplicate; the buoy outvoted it. Traffic navigates by the buoy and files by the record, which is why the audits never reconcile.

discoveryPlate.title: Lost Freight Apron
discoveryPlate.body: Six racks of bonded crates in a slow orbit of their own claim tag. Every crate is filed as in-transit to a berth that closed in the last expansion. Nothing here is legally lost, so nothing here may be legally opened.

discoveryPlate.title: Overtime Berth
discoveryPlate.body: A yard tug parked nose-in on a berth marker, drive cold, tow line still made fast to nothing. Her shift ticket is open and accruing. The yard stopped paying into it years ago; nobody has found the form that ends a shift retroactively.

discoveryPlate.title: Seam Tag 19
discoveryPlate.body: Stencil paint on the outer field’s biggest rock: a hull mark, three tally strokes, and a date nobody files anymore. The starter crews tag the seam they learned on; the nineteenth tag is the one that stuck, because the eighteenth is on a rock somebody mined.

discoveryPlate.title: Pilgrim Mooring
discoveryPlate.body: A mooring buoy a watch off the Candle Fleet where the family rafts tie up on the convoy’s date. Ribbons, chalk names, a thermos left for a father who isn’t coming back for it. The harbour master logs the moorings and never counts them.

stations.name: Ceres Refinery
stations.chartNote: Refinery row — buys ore dear, sells plates cheap, and the yard desk always needs another run moved.

stations.name: Belt Outpost
stations.chartNote: Rock crews and a scale. Ore moves same-shift; nothing else does.

discoveryPlate.title: Sold Twice
discoveryPlate.body: A head-class rig abandoned bit-down on a face it never cracked. The Ceres yard records list it sold for scrap twice. The armor plating bolted over its survey lamps is presumably the second buyer’s work.

discoveryPlate.title: Refinery Flare Rack
discoveryPlate.body: The crackers' burn-off, racked and shielded so the arrival queue can read it from a belt away — the first light on the leg in from the Helios gate. When the rack goes dark the row is on safety hold and the scale closes with it.

discoveryPlate.title: Inbound Weigh Pin
discoveryPlate.body: The refinery queue's tally post. Chalk rows list berth times by shift — eighteen minutes on a good one. The oldest row has been scratched out and rewritten so many times the plate is now a hole.

pois.name: RUCKUS · Open Work Order
pois.chartNote: An old demolition retriever is keeping one pressure core. Scan to hail. Massline the core and throw it.

discoveryPlate.title: RU-7 / Open Work Order
discoveryPlate.body: The crew clocks stopped. The retrieval service did not. Scan to wake RUCKUS; throw his caged core with the Massline. Three returns earn a pressure present. A held line pauses its countdown. Keep clear of the amber ring.

discoveryPlate.title: Kettle Line — First Overboard
discoveryPlate.body: A loaded piece of the Kettle Line, torn loose right off the gate approach with its pallet straps still knotted. The Line worked this seam for eleven years; this is the first piece the belt ever gave back.

discoveryPlate.title: Kettle Line — Sheared Ribs
discoveryPlate.body: Rib clusters and pod frames sheared inward, against the convoy’s own run. Whatever took the Kettle Line did it from open dark, without running a light or asking. The Belt Outpost logged nothing that night.

discoveryPlate.title: Kettle Line — the Stern That Refused
discoveryPlate.body: The Kettle Line’s drive stern, its bell slagged from the inside: the engineers blew the drive rather than let the attacker tow the convoy home. The pay strongbox is still clamped where the bosun welded it. The attacker got nothing; the belt kept the rest.

discoveryPlate.title: SL-9 / The Star Lantern
discoveryPlate.body: An ancient gyroscopic astronomical lantern turning on the cold rim of Ceres Belt. Three floating focus prisms orbit its captive stellar heart. Scan to hail; ride the beam to recharge, or tether the prisms into alignment to ignite the lantern.

pois.name: Claim Forty-Tag
pois.chartNote: Worked claim, stamps legible. The tally post on the inbound leg lists its shift.

discoveryPlate.title: Claim Forty-Tag
discoveryPlate.body: A claim pin seated in drilled rock, its stamp plate still legible under the dust: FORTY-TAG, Drift Shift Board, third issue. The rock it marks has been worked to the face and back — someone kept this claim alive through three crews by paying the filing fee on time, every time.

discoveryPlate.title: Re-stake on Forty
discoveryPlate.body: A second claim pin driven four hands from the first, stamped fourth issue over the third. The Board lapsed the claim when the crew missed two tallies, then re-filed it to their replacement the same shift. The rock never knew the difference. The families did.

pois.name: Ash Pin on the Pallas Leg
pois.chartNote: Burned claim pin. Still pings a survey ID. Nobody answers to it.

discoveryPlate.title: Ash Pin on the Pallas Leg
discoveryPlate.body: A claim pin cooked down to its socket by whatever took the crew — hull burn, drive flash, the record is one line long. The pin still transmits its survey ID on the old band. Drift crews pass it slow. Not from superstition: the ID is still on the Board’s books, and the books are what the belt has instead of graves.

discoveryPlate.title: Cathedral Vigil
discoveryPlate.body: A worklight tower parked on the Cathedral approach, lamps pointed in, power cell swapped on a schedule nobody ordered. Under the mounting plate someone welded two names from the Second Measure’s manifest — Okafor, Breen — because the shipbreak’s own tally reads only tonnage.

discoveryPlate.title: Lapsed Claim Cache
discoveryPlate.body: A sacked assay locker tucked under a spun-out claim rock, pin still mounted above it. The ore inside was weighed, tagged, and never collected — the crew’s toll receipt is dated three weeks before the Board struck their claim. The rock keeps what the dead already paid for.

discoveryPlate.title: Short-Ration Pod
discoveryPlate.body: A provisions pod off the Belt Outpost approach, missed by the skiff that was supposed to catch it and logged as delivered anyway. The manifest says forty ration bricks. The outpost’s mess board says the crew ate paste that week. Both records are correct.

discoveryPlate.title: SHAFT 7
discoveryPlate.body: A Drift Miners claim stake filed SHAFT 7, SEAM LEDGER PAGE GONE. Nine of eleven crews came back from the cave-in; the stake marks the cut, not the rescue. Belt crews touch it for luck they don’t name.

discoveryPlate.title: Three-Lamp Corner
discoveryPlate.body: A survey lamp rig the shift abandoned mid-tear-down — two lamps dead, one still burning on battery years past its rating. The refinery lists it as navigation furniture now; the crew list says it was supposed to come home on the second skiff.

pois.name: Rookery Prospect

discoveryPlate.title: Rookery Prospect — Staked Twice, Worked Once
discoveryPlate.body: A DMC survey stake from the first belt rush, re-flagged when Ceres Refinery opened intake. The rig log shows one shift cut and one pay-out before the crew walked to a richer seam; the on-site scale still reads the last tare.

pois.why: A first-rush DMC survey stake, worked one shift and walked off when the seam thinlined. Your flag is the third on this rock.

stations.name: Tethys Trade Hub
stations.chartNote: Convoys, patrols, and sealed freight change hands under the live DMC–MTS front board.

stations.name: Customs Gate
stations.chartNote: Toll plate and a scanner. Everything transits; nothing transits unread.

discoveryPlate.title: The Tally Post — WT-TETH-19
discoveryPlate.body: Meridian gold on a Concord frame. Every hull inbound from Helios crosses the scan gate and holds open for count here; the queue lamps run group-of-three for the standard limit. The desk codes it WT-TETH-19 — the lane just calls it the Tally.

discoveryPlate.title: Held, For Count
discoveryPlate.body: Nine racks of bonded freight the Tally desk seized and never finished counting. The desk still codes them pending; the queue lamps have outlived three desk supervisors. Nothing here has been legally lost, which is why nobody has legally taken it.

discoveryPlate.title: Exhibit A
discoveryPlate.body: One pod off a hauler that ran the gate dark. The seizure stamp is still legible; the manifest is not. It sits where the desk can see it, which is where the desk wants it.

pois.name: RUBRIC · The Marking Line
pois.chartNote: A hull marker will not mark a moving hull. Scan to read its work; put a line on the hull and bring it to rest.

discoveryPlate.title: HM-11 / The Marking Line
discoveryPlate.body: A retired Customs Gate stencil drone hangs hull F-41 on a slack line south of the count rack. The hull is filed CLEARED. The drone has painted a different answer beside it. Scan to read its work; it will not mark a moving hull, so put a line on the hull and bring it to rest.

pois.name: Convoy Marshal Nine
pois.chartNote: Outbound marshal buoy. Convoys form on its lamps before the Reach run.

discoveryPlate.title: Convoy Marshal Nine
discoveryPlate.body: A Meridian marshal buoy on the Io corridor, painted over a Concord lane keeper whose serial still bleeds through. Outbound hulls form on its lamps in groups of three — the same count grammar the Tally runs inbound, reversed. Its log lists every convoy that ever left on time. The log is a short file.

discoveryPlate.title: Form-Up Post
discoveryPlate.body: The convoy assembly tally. Chalk columns list hull counts by departure window — three deep is standard, four is a good week, five means somebody is lying about their manifest. The post has never once been written on by the desk it belongs to.

discoveryPlate.title: Refused Consignment
discoveryPlate.body: A bonded pod set off-lane after the form-up count found a mass the manifest declined to mention. It carries two tags: the marshal’s REFUSED stamp and the consignee’s address correction, filed four cycles ago, still pending. The refusal is the only complete document on board.

pois.name: Second Count Buoy
pois.chartNote: Dead Concord count station. The Meridian toll is the second one this lane has paid.

discoveryPlate.title: Second Count Buoy
discoveryPlate.body: A Concord count buoy, decommissioned when the lane lease changed hands. Its lamps are dark but the mount is still standing and the seal is still on the housing — the desk that retired it filed the shutdown, filed the salvage order, and filed the waiver when nobody came. The Vesta leg paid a toll before it paid this one. It will pay another after.

discoveryPlate.title: The Re-filed Hull
discoveryPlate.body: A short-haul freighter flagged HELD where the lane used to bend. The customs desk that seized her was re-filed twice — first as a Meridian annex, then as a line item — and the hold order transferred with the furniture. Her crew signed the release forms years ago. The hold did not.

discoveryPlate.title: Braid Tally
discoveryPlate.body: A weigh-post on the braid’s inner field where three lanes’ worth of ore changes hands informally. The post’s brass plate is worn to the grain; the tally marks are fresh every shift, and none of them are filed.

stages.label: The Stepwell · Extract the two ballast steps and tow each to its opposite socket. Seating both steps quiets the gulf recoil.
The Glass Harp · Cut and release the three bent harp chords. Each chord is a real free mass; the last one quiets the fissure.
GALLEY WARM · PACK RELEASED · RACK EMPTY
GALLEY WARM · EMERGENCY PACK BACK ON ITS RACK
GALLEY WARM · PACK POWERS LOADING LAMP · SPARE RACK EMPTY
The Ship Inside the Ice · Cut the keel seam, release its clamp and tow the finite keel into the shore cradle. The shoal opens.
The Ship Inside the Ice · SECURED
The Unwritten Bridge · Cut and release both bridge spans. The fence wind stops when the second clamp opens.
The Last Lantern · Restore power, focus the dish, then light the lantern. The shadow intake releases its hold.
The Red Sun Engine · Repair the bleed valve, cut the hot core free and tow it to the cold socket to stop the ash wall.
